external_evidence: Backtrace in the report: abort() in AWS-LC rand_bytes_core (rand.c) <- RAND_bytes <- aws_lc_rs::rand::fill <- rustls SessionId::random <- rustls ClientConnection::new. Reporter attributes it to AWS-LC's aarch64 RNDR path (rndr-armv8.pl) which does not retry a transient RNDR failure, and points to upstream aws/aws-lc#3453. The uv certificates doc confirms uv's TLS stack is rustls with aws-lc-rs as the crypto provider, so the abort originates in that dependency. The workaround (OPENSSL_armcap=~0x20000) disables the RNDR path and reportedly removes the aborts.
rationale: The report is a hard crash (SIGABRT, exit 134) in uv on aarch64 cold-cache downloads, so it is a bug in the sense that uv's process dies, but the fix belongs upstream in AWS-LC (rustls/aws-lc-rs provider), so likely_external is true. The backtrace, version, platform and upstream reference are enough for a maintainer to act without a reproduction, so needs_mre is false. Searches for SIGABRT/RNDR/AWS-LC/rustls abort/exit 134 returned no earlier issues, so no duplicates or related issues are listed; the uv docs (certificates page) confirm the rustls + aws-lc-rs stack. Confidence is medium because the hardware-specific intermittent behaviour was not verified by any tool.
